# Implement a ready item and review every version

## Intent

A work item whose plan is settled has to become code that can be trusted
without a person reading every line. nightshift has an implementer session
implement the item's package in the item's task fork, takes as done only
what the hub and the fork show, runs the package's gate on every version of
the item's change, has a reviewer with a fresh context review every gated
version, sends work back to the implementer as findings until gate and
reviewer agree, and asks the person only where it cannot go on by itself: a
version that touches a blocked path, and a reviewer and an implementer who
do not come to terms.

## Goals

- **A `ready` item is implemented without the person.** nightshift opens the
  item's change, starts the implementer with `af-impl`, and moves the item
  through `implementing` and `reviewing` to `landing`.
- **A session is believed only as far as the hub confirms it.** A session
  counts when the change has a new version and the package on that version
  has no open task, whatever the session says of itself.
- **Every version is gated and reviewed.** The package's gate runs as the
  session user on a clone of the fork at the version and is reported to the
  hub as the check `nightshift-gate`; the reviewer's verdict is reported as
  `nightshift-review`. Neither check is carried over to another version by
  nightshift.
- **Work is sent back as findings.** A failed gate, a reviewer's objection,
  a person's comment and, from later packages, a conflict report or a failed
  health command start the implementer in rework mode; its replies are
  written to the thread.
- **A reviewer's verdict is a check, never an approval.** An approval a
  policy rule requires stays a person's.
- **A blocked path stops the item at the push.** The item waits on a
  `blocked` decision before the gate runs.
- **Disagreement ends with the person.** After 3 reviews without `agree` the
  item waits on a `review_disagreement` decision.
- **Files outside the plan are noted, not held.**
- **A fork does not expire under running work, and expired work is
  restored.** The fork's lifetime is extended while the item waits on no
  decision; a fork that expired while it did is replaced when the person
  answers.
- **An item waits for the packages it depends on.**

## Background

Packages 01 to 05 leave a daemon that registers workspaces, takes in work
items, plans a defect or a change request into a spec package on a task
fork with a draft change, and can run sessions under a scheduler. Nothing
implements a package yet. The Go packages `internal/impl`, `internal/gate`
and `internal/review` are new.

What this package uses of Parley, as its `docs/api.md` states at commit
`7eabfb9`:

- A **change** records a version for every head its source branch has while
  it is draft or open. `GET …/changes/{number}` answers the current
  `version`, `head_sha`, `base_sha`, `state`, `paths` (the files the current
  version touches, at most 2,000) and `landing` with its `requirements`,
  each with `rule`, `paths` (the first 50), `checks`, `block` and
  `satisfied`; `include=versions,overlaps` adds the versions and the overlap
  entries. A draft never lands; `PATCH …/changes/{number}` with
  `{"state":"open"}` marks it ready.
- A change cannot be opened for a branch that has no commit its target
  lacks (`400 nothing_to_land`), so an imported package's change exists only
  after the implementer's first push.
- `PUT …/changes/{number}/checks/{name}` reports a check on a `version`
  with `status` and a `summary` of at most 2,000 characters; it needs the
  scope `checks:write`, and a later report for the same version and name
  replaces the earlier one.
- `GET …/changes/{number}/diff?version=<n>&format=patch` answers a version's
  diff against its base as patch text, cut at 8 MiB with the header
  `X-Parley-Truncated: true`.
- The head of every version stays at
  `refs/parley/changes/<number>/<version>` in the target workspace's
  repository, also after the fork is gone, and a fork reads its parent's
  objects, so a branch of a new fork can be created at an earlier version's
  head with `POST …/scm/refs`.
- A fork lives until its `expires_at`; `PATCH /api/v1/workspaces/{fork}`
  with `ttl` sets it to now plus `ttl`. Removing a fork abandons its draft
  and open changes.
- `GET …/scm/file` and `GET …/scm/tree` read a file and a directory at a
  revision, with the scope `git:read`.
- Two changes **overlap** when both are draft or open, have the same target
  branch and touch a file in common; the hub tracks it about a second
  behind a push.

What it uses of `agent-fox-dev/spec`: `afspec.LoadSpec` and
`Spec.IsFinished`; a task's `touches` and the plan's `dependencies`;
`speca <package> --gate full`, which runs the package's `linter` and
`all_tests` and answers one JSON object whose `result.gate.verdict` is
`pass`, `fail` or `not_run`; and `af-impl` in the modes PRD 09 of that
repository specifies (`--no-merge`, `--rework`, `--result`), which its
skill does not have yet on 2026-11-28 (packages 30 and 31 of that
repository are active with every task pending).

## Requirements

Constraint: Linux and macOS; Windows is best effort. Constraint: `speca` is
installed on the daemon's machine where the session user finds it on
`PATH`.

### Configuration

| Key | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `[gate].timeout` | how long one command of a gate may run | `30m` |

A value that is not greater than zero fails the start check `config`
(`config: gate.timeout must be greater than 0`).

### Scheduling: dependencies and overlaps

A `ready` item does not start while a package it depends on (the
`dependencies` of its `tasks.json`) is not finished on the default branch.
Items do not wait for each other because of the files they touch. When the
hub reports that an item's change overlaps another open change, nightshift
notes it once in the item's thread with the other change's number.

A dependency is finished when the package with that number in `.specs/` at
the tip of the workspace's default branch loads and `IsFinished` says so; a
package that is not there is not finished. `nightshift item show` names
what the item waits for: `package 03 on main`.

### Implementation

For a `ready` item nightshift creates the task fork and the draft change,
unless planning created them, opens the change (it is a draft no longer),
and starts an implementer session that implements the item's package with
`af-impl`, told to stop at the pushed branch (`af-impl <package>
--unattended --no-merge --result <file>`). The session commits on the
change's branch and pushes it to the fork; it merges nothing and calls no
forge. Every push records a version of the change.

An imported package has no commit on its branch before the implementer's
first push, and the hub opens no change for such a branch. For such an
item nightshift creates the fork, and opens the change, not as a draft,
when the first session ended and its branch is on the fork.

The item is `ready` until its first implementer session starts, and
`implementing` from then on.

When the session ends, nightshift reads from the hub and the fork, not from
the session's account: the change has a version newer than at the session's
start, and the package on that version has no task `pending` or
`in_progress`. When either does not hold, the session counts as failed with
the reason (`no new version`, `tasks still open`). A session that left no
result file counts as failed with the reason `no result`.

**Sending work back.** Wherever the source PRD says the implementer is
started with something (a failed gate's verdict, the reviewer's findings,
the person's comment, a conflict report, a failed health command's output),
it is started as a rework of the package (`af-impl <package> --unattended
--rework <findings file> --result <file>`), each of those written as a
finding. A comment of the person, and a finding the person made binding,
must be fixed, not answered. The session's replies, one per finding, are
written to the thread. A rework that changed nothing, or failed, counts as
a failed session.

The findings file is a JSON array; a finding has `id`, `source` (`gate`,
`review`, `person`, `health` or `conflict`), `text` and, where there are
any, `file`, `line`, `criterion`, `output` and `binding`.

nightshift then runs the package's gate on the version (`speca`'s gate, on a
clone of the fork at that version) and reports it to the hub as the check
`nightshift-gate`, `passed` or `failed`, with the verdict's summary. On
`failed` the implementer is started again with the verdict; this counts
toward the two attempts of *Roles and sessions* of the source PRD.

After every new version nightshift reads the hub's evaluation of it:

- when a requirement of it blocks, the item waits at once on a decision of
  kind `blocked`, naming the rule and the files; its options are `revise`
  (with a comment, required; the implementer is started with it) and
  `abandon` (package 09 adds `take_over`);
- the files of the version that the package's tasks did not name in
  `touches` are listed in one thread entry, `outside the plan: <files>`
  (the first 50). Nothing is held back for them.

Open items the session's result file lists (what `af-impl` calls `unmet`,
the member `open_items`) each become a new work item of kind `defect` in
state `new`, linked to the item they came from, and are listed in the
thread. Such an item stays `new`, with no session, until the person runs
`nightshift item plan <N>` (package 05).

**A fork that expired.** nightshift extends the lifetime of an item's fork
while the item does not wait on a decision. While it does, the fork may
expire on the hub. When the person then answers, nightshift creates a new
fork and a new change: for an item `awaiting_approval`, from the package
text it kept; for any other, from the last version the hub recorded of the
earlier change. The thread names both changes, and the gate and the review
run again on the new one.

### Review of a change

When `nightshift-gate` passed on a version, the item is `reviewing`. The
reviewer session reads the package, the diff of the version against its
base and the gate's verdict, with a token that can read the fork and
nothing else. Its verdict is `agree` or `object`, with findings that each
name a file and a line or a criterion. A later review of the same item is
given the earlier findings with the implementer's replies as well.

On `agree`, nightshift reports the check `nightshift-review` as `passed` on
that version, and the item is `landing`. On `object`, it reports `failed`,
and the implementer is started with the findings; its new version is gated
and reviewed again. After 3 reviews of one item without `agree`, the item
waits on a decision of kind `review_disagreement`, showing each open
finding with the implementer's reply; its options are `side_with_reviewer`
(the implementer gets one more session with the findings marked as
binding), `side_with_implementer` (`nightshift-review` is reported
`passed`, the summary naming the person's decision) and `abandon` (package
09 adds `take_over`).

nightshift never records an approval on the hub for a model's verdict: a
model's review is a check, so that an approval a policy rule requires stays
a person's.

### What this package offers the later ones

Packages 07 to 10 use these, by these names:

- **`internal/impl`, `(*impl.Service).Rework(ctx, item int, findings
  []impl.Finding) error`**: the rework entry point. It keeps the findings
  for the item's next implementer session and moves an item that is
  `reviewing` or `landing` to `implementing`; the version the rework
  produces is evaluated, gated and reviewed again. `impl.Finding` has `ID`,
  `Source`, `Text`, `File`, `Line`, `Criterion`, `Output` and `Binding`;
  an empty `ID` is given one.
- **`(*impl.Service).SetClass(ctx, item int, class sched.Class) error`**:
  the class every later session of the item is asked with (a repair:
  `sched.ClassRepair`).
- **`(*impl.Service).ReportCheck(ctx, item int, name, status, summary
  string) error`**: reports a check on the current version of the item's
  change and writes the thread entry.
- **`(*impl.Service).Version(ctx, item int) (impl.Version, error)`**: the
  item's change as the hub has it now: `Workspace`, `Change`, `Number`,
  `HeadSHA`, `BaseSHA`, `State`, `Paths`, `Requirements` and `Overlaps`.
- **`(*impl.Service).OpenBlocked(ctx, item int, reqs
  []impl.Requirement) error`**: opens the `blocked` decision, for a block
  the hub reports at a land.
- **`(*impl.Service).RestoreFork(ctx, item int) error`**: restores an
  expired fork and does nothing for one the hub still has; a step of a
  later package calls it before it uses the fork.
- **`(*impl.Service).OnAnswer(kind, option, fn)`**: registers an answer's
  handler with the inbox so that, for a paused item, the answer is kept
  and carried out at the resume.
- **`(*impl.Service).OutsidePlan(ctx, item int) ([]string, error)`**: the
  files of the item's last evaluated version outside its plan.
- **`internal/gate`, `gate.Run(ctx, gate.Options) (gate.Verdict, error)`**
  and the names `gate.CheckName` (`nightshift-gate`) and
  `review.CheckName` (`nightshift-review`).
- **`internal/hub`**: `(*hub.Client).Change`, `SetChangeState`,
  `ReportCheck`, `ChangeDiff`, `File`, `Tree`, `CreateRef`, `Commit` and
  `SetForkTTL`.

### What this package uses of package 05

- `change.Service.Get(ctx, item)`: the item's `Record` with `Workspace`,
  `Fork` (the fork's slug), `GitURL`, `Branch` (`item-<N>`), `Generation`,
  `Change` (0 while the item has no change), `ChangeRef` and `ChangeURL`;
  `change.ErrNotFound` for an item without a fork.
- `change.Service.EnsureFork(ctx, item)`: creates the item's task fork
  where it has none.
- `change.Service.OpenDraft(ctx, item, title, intent, sessionID)`: opens
  the draft change for the item's branch.
- `change.Service.Forget(ctx, item)`: after it, `EnsureFork` creates a new
  fork for the item (`<workspace>--i<N>-<g>`).
- `change.Service.Abandon(ctx, item, reason)`, which package 05 registers
  as the abandon hook.
- `plan.Service.Kept(ctx, item)`: for a planned item the package's
  directory (`Dir`, `.specs/NN_name`) and the kept text (`Files`, by path
  below `Dir`).
- `plan.Service.RegisterPrepare(name, fn)`: a function package 05 calls
  before it carries out an answer `approve` or `revise` to a `plan`
  decision; while it returns an error the answer waits. This package
  registers the fork's restore there.

### End-to-end flows

**A ready item reaches `landing`.** Item 12 is `ready` with a draft change
from its planning, and the package it depends on is finished on `main`.
nightshift opens the change and asks for an implementer session; when it
starts, the item is `implementing`. The implementer pushes, which records
version 2, and writes its result file. nightshift finds the new version and
no open task, creates one `defect` item from the result's open item, reads
the hub's evaluation, notes `outside the plan: docs/api.md`, runs the gate
and reports `nightshift-gate` `passed`; the item is `reviewing`. The
reviewer agrees; `nightshift-review` is reported `passed`; the item is
`landing`. The hub holds no approval.

**A reviewer who does not agree.** The reviewer objects to version 2 of
item 13; the implementer reworks it, and its replies are in the thread.
The reviewer objects to version 3 and to version 4. A
`review_disagreement` decision appears in `nightshift inbox --action` with
the findings and the replies. The person runs `nightshift decide <id>
--option side_with_implementer`; `nightshift-review` is reported `passed`
on version 4 with the summary naming the decision, and the item is
`landing`.

**A blocked path, and a fork that expired meanwhile.** The implementer's
version of item 14 touches `secrets/key.pem`, which a rule blocks. The item
waits on a `blocked` decision naming the rule and the file; no gate ran.
The fork expires on the hub. Days later the person answers `revise` with a
comment. nightshift creates a new fork and a new change at the last
version's head and names both changes in the thread; the implementer
reworks with the comment as a binding finding; the new version no longer
touches the file, is gated and goes to review.

## Design Decisions

From the source PRD, by its numbers:

- **4. Files outside the plan are noted, not held.** The owner decided it.
- **15. A fork may expire while its item waits on the person; nightshift
  restores the work when they answer.** The owner decided it.
- **18. Items never wait for each other on files.** The owner decided it;
  an overlap is a note.
- **20, 21. The reviewer works in a fresh context and reviews every
  change; the implementer runs on `claude -p` with `af-impl`.** The owner
  decided it.
- **24. nightshift opens the change; a session's token cannot.** Chosen
  there.
- **27. A blocked path stops the item at the push.** Chosen there.
- **30. Open items a session reports become unplanned `defect` items.**
  Kept from PRD 01.
- **31. 3 review rounds and 2 attempts per step** are starting values.
- **36. Work is sent back through `af-impl`'s rework mode, and every
  session reports through a result file.** The owner decided the first.
- **40. A person's pushed version is gated and reviewed as an agent's.**
  Chosen there.
- **41. The gate runs as the session user.** Chosen there.

Chosen here:

1. **Three Go packages: `internal/gate` (run `speca`'s gate in a directory
   and read its verdict), `internal/impl` (everything from `ready` to a
   gated version, the findings, the forks, the `blocked` decision) and
   `internal/review` (the review step and `review_disagreement`), which
   imports `impl`.** Why: the split's table puts `blocked` with the review,
   but the evaluation that opens it runs before the gate, in `impl`, and
   `review` needs `impl`'s rework entry point.
2. **What a step does is decided from the hub's state and the stored
   findings, in a fixed order, not from where the previous call stopped.**
   Why: a restart, a pause, a restored fork and a version a person pushed
   then need no case of their own.
3. **The item moves to `implementing` when its first implementer session
   starts, which nightshift learns from the event `session.started` of the
   event log.** Why: the source PRD keeps an item `ready` while it waits
   for a free session, the daily limit or a dependency, and package 04's
   start order and guards apply to a session asked for a `ready` item.
4. **The package of a version is read from the hub (`GET …/scm/tree` and
   `…/scm/file` at the version's head) into a temporary directory and
   loaded with `afspec.LoadSpec`; "no task `pending` or `in_progress`" is
   `IsFinished`.** Why: "from the hub, not from the session's account", and
   the daemon's user need not read the session user's files.
5. **A session's acceptance is package 04's accept function: `no new
   version`, `tasks still open` and `package does not load: <reason>` are
   its errors.** A rework that changed nothing or failed is recognised the
   same way: the change has no newer version, reason `no new version`.
6. **Replies are written to the thread from every rework's result file,
   also from a rework that is not accepted.** Why: a declined finding is an
   answer the person and the reviewer should see.
7. **Findings wait in the store until a rework session that was given them
   is accepted. While the package has an open task, the implementer is
   started with `--no-merge`, and the findings wait for the rework after
   it.** Why: `af-impl --rework` refuses a package with open tasks.
8. **Finding ids are `f<n>`, counted per item.**
9. **The gate is `speca <package> --gate full --timeout <gate.timeout>`,
   run with `sh -c` through `command.Runner` in a clone at
   `<sessions.dir>/items/<N>/gate`, with `XDG_STATE_HOME` set to an empty
   directory of that run, its JSON written to a file read through package
   04's file read.** Why: the session user owns the state directory in
   which `speca` records passes for reuse, so a pass recorded there is the
   session's account; a fresh directory makes every gate run its commands.
10. **Everything but the verdict `pass` is reported as `failed`**: `fail`,
    `not_run`, a `speca` that exits other than 0 or cannot be found, output
    that does not parse, and a run past twice the timeout plus one minute.
    Why: the check has two values, and a gate that did not run proves
    nothing.
11. **The check's summary is `speca`'s `summary`, then for a failure the
    failing command's name, its exit code and its `tail`, cut to 2,000
    characters.**
12. **A failed gate is recorded with `Scheduler.RecordFailure` for the step
    `implement`; when two gates in a row fail for an item with no passed
    gate between them, nightshift opens `session_failed` with
    `Scheduler.OpenSessionFailed`.** Why: package 04 sets its count to zero
    when the rework session completes, so two failed gates would otherwise
    never be "two attempts".
13. **A file is inside the plan when a `touches` entry equals its path or
    names a directory above it, or when it lies in the package's own
    directory.** Why: `touches` names files, packages and modules, and
    every implementation writes the package's `progress.json`.
14. **The `outside the plan` entry is written for a version when the list
    is not empty and differs from the one last written for the item.**
    Why: a rework that adds no file should not repeat it.
15. **Overlaps are read after each gate, and each other change is noted
    once per item** (`overlaps change demo#7`). Why: the hub tracks an
    overlap behind the push, and the gate gives it the time.
16. **A `blocked` decision is opened once per version.**
17. **An answer is carried out by its handler at once, and at the resume
    for a paused item** (`Scheduler.Paused`, `Scheduler.OnResume`).
18. **`revise` is the recommended option of `blocked`,
    `side_with_reviewer` of `review_disagreement`.**
19. **A reviewer's finding that names neither a file with a line nor a
    criterion fails the review session** (`finding names no file and line
    and no criterion`), through the accept function.
20. **The reviewer's prompt holds the package's directory, the list of
    changed files, the diff up to 400,000 characters (then a line saying
    how much was left out), the gate's summary, and the earlier findings
    with their replies.** Why: the reviewer has no shell and cannot produce
    a diff, and reads the rest in its clone at the version's head.
21. **The count of reviews without `agree` is the number of `object`
    verdicts since the item's last `agree`; an answer does not set it
    back.** Why: after the person sided with the reviewer once, a further
    objection should reach them at once.
22. **The fork's lifetime is set to `7d` every 6 hours** for every item
    that has a fork, is neither `done` nor `abandoned` and waits on no
    decision. Why: 7 days is the hub's default and inside every maximum it
    can be configured with.
23. **An expired fork is noticed by `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{fork}`
    answering `404`**, at three moments: when a decision of the item is
    answered (the event `decision.answered`, unless the option is
    `abandon`), before package 05 carries out an answer to a `plan`
    decision (`plan.Service.RegisterPrepare`), and at the start of every
    step of this package. Why: the answer of a kind another package
    declared has to restore the fork too, and a daemon that was stopped
    for longer than the lifetime has no answer to react to.
24. **The restored change is opened as the earlier one was: a draft for an
    item that is `new`, `planning` or `awaiting_approval`, open otherwise;
    an item that was `reviewing` or `landing` returns to `implementing`.**
    Why: "the gate and the review run again on the new one".
25. **An open item's text is its `title`, `missing`, `why` and `closes`,
    cut to 20,000 characters; an open item whose title a linked item of
    the same parent already has creates none.** Why: an accept that runs
    twice must not create two items.
26. **Thread entries: `check`, `reply`, `outside_plan`, `overlap` and
    `fork_restored`; none marks the thread unread.**
27. **No route and no command.** Everything of this package is reached
    through the inbox and the item commands of packages 03 and 04.

## Dependencies

- **`01_daemon_api_and_credentials`** (status `draft`): the configuration
  struct, the store's migrations, the hub client, `internal/hubtest`, the
  event log with `Subscribe`, the e2e helper.

  …/scm/commits`; `POST …/changes` refusing `nothing_to_land`; that
  `changes:write` satisfies `changes:read` and `git:write` `git:read`.
  **Not read:** the status of `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}` for a fork
  that was removed (assumed `404`), and the member names of a `scm/tree`
  list.

  `Spec.PRDBody`.

  repository specifies them; `af-impl --unattended` exists.

## Glossary

- **version**: one head of the source branch of an item's change, as the
  hub numbered it.
- **gate**: the package's `linter` and `all_tests`, run by `speca`.
- **finding**: one thing the implementer must fix or answer: from the gate,
  the reviewer, the person, a conflict or the health command.
- **binding**: a finding that must be fixed, not answered.
- **rework**: an implementer session in `af-impl`'s rework mode, given
  findings.
- **reply**: the implementer's answer to one finding: `fixed`, `declined`,
  `not_reproduced` or `failed`, with a text.
- **evaluation**: the hub's `landing` of a change's current version: which
  policy rules its files select and what each requires.
- **outside the plan**: a file of a version that no task's `touches`
  names.
- **open item** (`unmet`): something an implementation left open, listed in
  the session's result file.
- **start guard**: a function registered with the scheduler that can
  refuse a session's start for an item, with a reason (package 04).
- **task fork, change, check, policy, overlap**: as Parley defines them.
- **package, `touches`, `dependencies`**: as the spec format of
  `agent-fox-dev/spec` defines them.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Start a ready item and accept its implementer session

**Rationale:** An approved plan should turn into a pushed version without the person, and a session's own account of its work is not evidence.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] WHILE a `ready` item's package names, in the `dependencies` of its `tasks.json`, a package that is not finished at the tip of the workspace's default branch: the directory with that number under `.specs/` there does not exist, does not load with `afspec.LoadSpec`, or `IsFinished` is false for it, THE nightshiftd SHALL refuse the item in the start guard `dependency`, registered with `Scheduler.RegisterGuard`, with the reason `package <NN> on <default branch>` naming the first such dependency in the plan's order; read the default branch from the hub (`GET …/scm/tree` of `.specs` and `GET …/scm/file` of the package's files at the workspace's `head_sha`) at most once in 30 seconds per workspace, an injected interval; and allow an item that is not `ready`, whose package names no dependency, or whose dependencies are all finished
   → the guard returns `(false, "package 03 on main", nil)` while the dependency is unfinished and `(true, "", nil)` at the first read after it is finished; an item that touches the same files as another is allowed; a hub error is returned as the guard's error, which the scheduler treats as a refusal
   Check: unit
   - setup: a fake hub (internal/hubtest) whose workspace `demo` serves `scm/tree` and `scm/file` from a repository fixture built with afspec
   - setup: an item 7 in `ready` whose package names the dependencies of the row
   - setup: an injected clock
   ```
   new file internal/impl/guard_test.go, a table over the default branch's .specs on the fake hub {03 with a pending task -> (false, 'package 03 on main'); 03 with every task done -> (true, ''); 03 sealed -> (true, ''); no directory 03_* -> (false, 'package 03 on main'); 03 whose tasks.json is not JSON -> (false, 'package 03 on main'); dependencies [02 done, 03 pending, 04 pending] -> names 03; no dependencies -> (true, ''); item in 'implementing' -> (true, '') without a hub request; hub stopped -> err != nil}: ok, reason, err = svc.DependencyGuard(ctx, item); assert as the row says. Then: advance the clock 10s and ask again -> the fake hub saw no further request; advance 30s -> it saw one
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] WHEN the scheduler calls the step of an item in `ready`, THE nightshiftd SHALL create the item's task fork with package 05's `change.Service.EnsureFork` where the item has none; set the item's change to open with `PATCH …/changes/{number}` `{"state":"open"}` where it is a draft; read the change's current version number, 0 for an item without a change; and, while the item is still `ready`, ask the scheduler for an implementer session with `session.Spec{Item, Role: implementer, Step: "implement", Fork, Branch, Prompt, Accept}`, the prompt being `/af-impl <package directory> --unattended --no-merge --result {result}`
   → the hub's change is `open` before the session is asked for; an item whose change is open already sends no `PATCH`; an imported package's item gets a fork and no change; the package directory is `source.dir` for an item of kind `spec` and `Dir` of package 05's `plan.Service.Kept` otherwise; when `RunSession` returns `sched.ErrNotStarted`, or a result whose outcome is not `completed`, the step returns nil and leaves the item's state as it is
   Check: integration
   - setup: a fake hub (internal/hubtest) holding the workspace `demo`, its forks, changes with versions, checks and a policy
   - setup: the impl service over the real item service, inbox, store and package 05's change service, a stub of its `plan.Service.Kept`, and a stub scheduler whose RunSession the test scripts and whose requests, RecordFailure and OpenSessionFailed calls it records
   ```
   new file internal/impl/start_test.go, a table over {planned item with a draft change 4 -> the fake hub saw PATCH changes/4 {state: open} before the request and no fork request; planned item whose change is open -> no PATCH; item of kind spec without a fork -> one fork created through EnsureFork, no change request; RunSession scripted to return sched.ErrNotStarted -> step returns nil and state == 'ready'; outcome 'failed' -> nil and state unchanged}: err = svc.Step(ctx, item); assert the recorded request == {Item, Role: 'implementer', Step: 'implement', Fork: rec.Fork, Branch: rec.Branch, Prompt: '/af-impl .specs/12_greeting --unattended --no-merge --result {result}'} and that its Accept is set
   ```
1. [REQ-1.3] WHEN the event `session.started` is appended to the event log for an implementer session of an item that is `ready`, THE nightshiftd SHALL move the item to `implementing` through the item service's `Transition`, with the reason `implementer session started`
   → the item's state is `implementing` and its thread has the entry `ready -> implementing: implementer session started`; a `session.started` of a planner or a reviewer, or of an item in another state, moves nothing and logs no error
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/impl/start_test.go, with the service following a real event log: a table over {implementer session of a ready item -> eventually state == 'implementing'; reviewer session of a ready item -> state stays 'ready'; implementer session of an item in 'implementing' -> unchanged, one `state` entry in all}: log.Append('session.started', {session, item, role}); assert as the row says
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] WHEN an implementer session asked with `--no-merge` has ended, the item's change on the hub has a version greater than at the session's start, and the package read from the hub at that version's head (`GET …/scm/file` of its `prd.md`, `requirements.json`, `tasks.json` and `progress.json`, loaded with `afspec.LoadSpec`) has no task `pending` or `in_progress`, THE nightshiftd SHALL accept the session by returning nil from the accept function, having first, for an item that had no change and whose branch is on the fork, opened the change through package 05's `change.Service.OpenDraft` with the item's title, the text of the package's `## Intent` section and the session's id, and set it open
   → the session's outcome is `completed` whatever `outcome` its result file names; an imported package's item has an open change at version 1 afterwards; the step goes on to the evaluation of that version in the same call
   Check: integration
   - setup: a fake hub (internal/hubtest) holding the workspace `demo`, its forks, changes with versions, checks and a policy
   - setup: the impl service over the real item service, inbox, store and package 05's change service, a stub of its `plan.Service.Kept`, and a stub scheduler whose RunSession the test scripts and whose requests, RecordFailure and OpenSessionFailed calls it records
   ```
   in internal/impl/start_test.go, RunSession scripted to push a commit to the fork's branch on the fake hub (which records the next version), mark every task of the package done there, and then call the request's Accept with a result file: a table over {planned item, change 4 at version 1, push -> version 2, result outcome 'complete' -> Accept returns nil; the same with result outcome 'gate_failed' -> nil; item of kind spec without a change, branch pushed -> Accept returns nil, the fake hub holds a change in state 'open' with the item's title and the package's intent, version 1}: assert Accept's error; assert the evaluation ran for that version (the stub evaluation hook saw it)
   ```
1. [REQ-1.5] IF an implementer session has ended and the item's change has no version greater than at the session's start (or the item has no change and its branch is not on the fork), or the package at the new version's head has a task `pending` or `in_progress`, or the package cannot be read from the hub or does not load, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL refuse the session by returning an error from the accept function, create no item from its result file, evaluate nothing and run no gate
   → the accept function's error is `no new version`, `tasks still open` or `package does not load: <first line of the error>`, which package 04 records as the failed session's reason; the item's state and its stored findings are unchanged; a session that left no result file is failed by package 04 with `no result` and the accept function is not called
   Check: unit
   - setup: a fake hub (internal/hubtest) holding the workspace `demo`, its forks, changes with versions, checks and a policy
   - setup: the impl service over the real item service, inbox, store and package 05's change service, a stub of its `plan.Service.Kept`, and a stub scheduler whose RunSession the test scripts and whose requests, RecordFailure and OpenSessionFailed calls it records
   ```
   in internal/impl/start_test.go, a table over {no push during the session -> 'no new version'; item of kind spec, branch not on the fork -> 'no new version'; push, task 2 pending at the head -> 'tasks still open'; push, task 2 in_progress -> 'tasks still open'; push, tasks.json at the head is not JSON -> starts with 'package does not load: '; result file says outcome 'complete' in every row}: err = req.Accept(result); assert err.Error() as the row says; assert count(items), the stored findings and the fake hub's check reports are unchanged
   ```
1. [REQ-1.6] WHEN an accepted implementer session's result file lists `open_items`, THE nightshiftd SHALL create for each entry, in the file's order, a work item with the item service's `CreateLinked(ctx, item, "defect", text)`, the text being the entry's `title`, then `missing`, `why` and `closes: <closes>` where they are present, each as a paragraph of its own, cut to 20,000 code points; and skip an entry whose title is the title of an item already linked to this parent
   → each new item is of kind `defect`, in `new`, with `parent` set, and the parent's thread has one `linked_item` entry for each; no session is asked for a new item; handling the same result file twice creates each item once; a result file without `open_items`, or with an empty list, creates none
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/impl/start_test.go: result = {outcome: 'complete_with_open_items', open_items: [{kind: 'defect', title: 'Log line missing', missing: 'm', why: 'w', closes: 'c'}, {kind: 'awaits', title: 'Waits for 09'}]}; svc.HandleResult(ctx, item, result); kids = items.Get(item).Children; assert len(kids) == 2; assert each has kind 'defect', state 'new'; assert the first's text == 'Log line missing\n\nm\n\nw\n\ncloses: c' and the second's == 'Waits for 09'; assert the parent's thread has two linked_item entries; assert the stub scheduler saw no request for a child; svc.HandleResult again -> still 2 children; a result without open_items -> no child
   ```

### REQ-2: Send work back to the implementer as findings

**Rationale:** A failed gate, an objection, a comment, a conflict and a failed health command all mean the same thing to the implementer: change the finished work, and say what was done about each point.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] WHEN a part of nightshift calls `(*impl.Service).Rework(ctx, item, findings)` with at least one finding, each with a `Text` that is not empty and a `Source` of `gate`, `review`, `person`, `health` or `conflict`, for an item in `ready`, `implementing`, `reviewing` or `landing`, THE nightshiftd SHALL store the findings in the given order after those already waiting for the item, giving each finding without an `ID` the next id `f<n>` of the item and setting `Binding` on every finding of the source `person`; move an item that is `reviewing` or `landing` to `implementing` with the reason `rework: <n> findings (<sources>)`; and wake the scheduler
   → returns nil; the findings are still waiting after a restart of the daemon; an item in `ready` or `implementing` keeps its state; a finding whose `ID` is already stored for the item is stored once, so a caller that is called twice may call twice
   Check: unit
   ```
   new file internal/impl/rework_test.go, a table over the item's state {ready, implementing, reviewing, landing}: err = svc.Rework(ctx, n, [{Source: 'review', Text: 'a', File: 'x.go', Line: 3}, {Source: 'person', Text: 'b'}]); assert err == nil; w = svc.Waiting(n); assert ids == ['f1','f2'] and w[1].Binding and not w[0].Binding; assert state == 'implementing' except for ready, which stays; for reviewing assert the thread's last entry == 'reviewing -> implementing: rework: 2 findings (review, person)'; assert the scheduler was woken. Then: Rework(n, [{ID: 'blocked-5', Source: 'person', Text: 'c'}]) twice -> one finding 'blocked-5', after f1 and f2; reopen the store -> svc.Waiting(n) is the same three
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] IF `Rework` is called with no finding, with a finding whose `Text` is empty or whose `Source` is none of the five, for an item nightshift does not know, or for an item in `new`, `planning`, `awaiting_approval`, `verifying`, `publishing`, `done` or `abandoned`, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL refuse the call, store no finding and leave the item's state as it is
   → the error satisfies `errors.Is` with `impl.ErrInvalid` for the findings, with the item service's `ErrNotFound` for the item and with `impl.ErrState` for the state; the count of stored findings and of thread entries is unchanged
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/impl/rework_test.go, a table over {findings nil -> ErrInvalid; [{Source: 'review', Text: ''}] -> ErrInvalid; [{Source: 'robot', Text: 'x'}] -> ErrInvalid; one good and one bad finding -> ErrInvalid and none stored; item 999 -> item.ErrNotFound; an item in each of the seven states -> ErrState}: err = svc.Rework(ctx, n, f); assert errors.Is(err, want); assert len(svc.Waiting(n)) and the thread's entry count unchanged
   ```
1. [REQ-2.3] WHEN the step of an `implementing` item runs, findings wait for the item, and the package at the head of the change's current version has no task `pending` or `in_progress`, THE nightshiftd SHALL ask the scheduler for an implementer session with the step `implement`, the prompt `/af-impl <package directory> --unattended --rework {input:findings} --result {result}` and the input `findings`: one JSON array of the waiting findings in their order, each an object with `id`, `source`, `text` and, where they are set, `file`, `line`, `criterion`, `output` and `binding`
   → the input parses as an array whose ids are those waiting, in order; a finding of the source `person` carries `"binding": true`; a member that is not set is absent, not empty; while the package has an open task the request is the `--no-merge` one of a first implementation and the findings stay waiting
   Check: integration
   - setup: a fake hub (internal/hubtest) holding the workspace `demo`, its forks, changes with versions, checks and a policy
   - setup: the impl service over the real item service, inbox, store and package 05's change service, a stub of its `plan.Service.Kept`, and a stub scheduler whose RunSession the test scripts and whose requests, RecordFailure and OpenSessionFailed calls it records
   ```
   in internal/impl/rework_test.go: Rework(n, [{Source: 'gate', Text: 'tests fail', Output: 'FAIL x'}, {Source: 'person', Text: 'keep the log line'}]); svc.Step(ctx, n); req = the recorded request; assert req.Step == 'implement'; assert req.Prompt == '/af-impl .specs/12_greeting --unattended --rework {input:findings} --result {result}'; assert json(req.Inputs['findings']) == [{id: 'f1', source: 'gate', text: 'tests fail', output: 'FAIL x'}, {id: 'f2', source: 'person', text: 'keep the log line', binding: true}]. Second case: task 2 of the package pending at the head -> req.Prompt holds '--no-merge' and no Inputs, and svc.Waiting(n) still has both
   ```
1. [REQ-2.4] WHEN a rework session has ended with a result file that lists `replies`, THE nightshiftd SHALL append to the item's thread, for each reply in the file's order, one entry of the kind `reply` with the text `<finding id> <action>: <text>`, cut to 2,000 characters and not marking the thread unread, and store the reply with the finding it names, whether or not the session is accepted afterwards
   → the thread has one `reply` entry per reply, in order, before the session's `session_ended` entry; the stored finding carries the reply's `action` and `text`; a reply that names no finding given to the session is written to the thread and stored with none
   Check: unit

1. [REQ-2.5] WHEN a rework session has ended and the item's change on the hub has a version greater than at the session's start, THE nightshiftd SHALL accept the session by returning nil from the accept function, take the findings that were given to it out of those waiting and keep them with their replies as the item's history, create the linked items of its `open_items` as for a first implementation, and go on to the evaluation of the new version
   → the session's outcome is `completed`; no finding given to it waits any longer; a finding stored while the session ran still waits and starts the next rework; the new version has no gate verdict and no review verdict
   Check: integration

   - setup: the impl service over the real item service, inbox, store and package 05's change service, a stub of its `plan.Service.Kept`, and a stub scheduler whose RunSession the test scripts and whose requests, RecordFailure and OpenSessionFailed calls it records

1. [REQ-2.6] IF a rework session has ended and the item's change has no version greater than at the session's start, THEN THE nightshiftd SHALL refuse the session by returning an error from the accept function and keep every finding that was given to it waiting
   → the accept function's error is `no new version`, which package 04 records as the failed session's reason, for a result file whose outcome is `nothing_changed`, `rework_failed` or `push_failed` alike; the next rework session is given the same findings; the item's state is unchanged
   Check: unit

1. [REQ-2.7] WHEN the scheduler calls the step of an item in `implementing`, THE nightshiftd SHALL do the first of these that applies, and then the next, until a session ended otherwise than `completed`, a decision of the item is open, an error occurred or the item has left `implementing`: restore the item's fork when the hub no longer has it; send a check report the hub has not taken and do what follows its verdict; start the implementer with `--no-merge` when the item has no change or the package at the change's head has an open task; start a rework when findings wait; evaluate the change's current version when it is not evaluated; run the gate when the version has no gate verdict; move the item to `reviewing` when the gate passed on the current version
   → what the step does depends only on the hub's change, the package at its head and what the store holds for the item, so a step called after a restart, a resume or a version a person pushed does what a first call would; a version whose gate failed and for which a finding waits starts a rework, not a second gate

   → the `Class` of each `sched.Request` for the item is the class set, `sched.ClassRepair` for a repair; an item with no class set is asked for with the zero class, so that the scheduler places it by its state; the class survives a restart


### REQ-3: Evaluate and gate every version

**Rationale:** A version that can never land should cost nothing more, and one that can has to pass the package's own checks on a clone the session did not prepare.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] WHEN nightshift reads the hub's evaluation of a version it has not evaluated (`GET …/changes/{number}` with `include=overlaps`) and a requirement of its `landing` has `block` true, THE nightshiftd SHALL open a decision of the kind `blocked` on the item's thread, with the question `Version <v> of item <N> touches paths that rule <rule> blocks. Revise it or abandon the item?`, as evidence the change's URL and, for each blocking requirement, the rule's name with the files that selected it, `revise` recommended and `item <N>` as what it blocks; record the version as evaluated; and run no gate on it
   → the kind `blocked` is declared in the inbox's registry with exactly the options `revise`, which requires a comment, and `abandon`; one decision is open per version however often the step runs; the item keeps its state and its `waiting_on` names the decision; the hub received no check report for that version
   Check: integration
   - setup: a fake hub (internal/hubtest) holding the workspace `demo`, its forks, changes with versions, checks and a policy
   - setup: the impl service over the real item service, inbox, store and package 05's change service, a stub of its `plan.Service.Kept`, and a stub scheduler whose RunSession the test scripts and whose requests, RecordFailure and OpenSessionFailed calls it records
   ```
   new file internal/impl/evaluate_test.go: the fake hub's policy blocks 'secrets/**'; version 2 of the item's change touches secrets/key.pem and api/greet.go; svc.Step(ctx, n) twice; d = the item's open decisions; assert len(d) == 1 and d[0].Kind == 'blocked'; assert option keys == ['revise','abandon'] with comment_required only on revise and revise recommended; assert the question == 'Version 2 of item 12 touches paths that rule nightshift-1 blocks. Revise it or abandon the item?'; assert the evidence names 'nightshift-1' and 'secrets/key.pem' and not 'api/greet.go'; assert items.Get(n).State == 'implementing' and its waiting_on.kind == 'blocked'; assert fakeHub.Checks(change) is empty and the gate stub was not called
   ```

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: A ready item is implemented, gated and reviewed up to landing

1. **nightshiftd** finds item 12 `ready` with a draft change and its dependency finished on `main`, opens the change and asks for an implementer session
2. **hub** marks the change open
3. **nightshiftd** starts the session and moves the item to `implementing`
4. **implementer** implements the package, pushes the branch and writes a result file with one open item
5. **hub** records version 2 of the change and evaluates it
6. **nightshiftd** accepts the session from the hub's version and the package's tasks, creates a `defect` item for the open item, writes `outside the plan: docs/api.md`, runs the gate and reports `nightshift-gate` passed; the item is `reviewing`
7. **reviewer** reads the package and the diff in a clone of its own and answers `agree`
8. **nightshiftd** reports `nightshift-review` passed on version 2 and moves the item to `landing`

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the nightshiftd run function with its scheduler, session service, item service, inbox, store and event log, internal/impl, internal/gate and internal/review with the real command runner and gitclone, package 05's change service against the fake hub, git against the fake hub's git endpoint

**Setup:**

- the daemon started in-process with the e2e helper of internal/daemon/e2e_test.go, sessions unisolated, against internal/hubtest
- a fake `claude` on PATH: a script the test writes that commits, marks the package's tasks done, pushes the branch and writes the result file the step's prompt names
- the reviewer's provider is a provider/faux client scripted with the verdicts of the flow
- a fake `speca` on PATH that prints a gate envelope with the verdict the test sets
- item 12 seeded `ready` with a fork, a branch holding an active package whose tasks touch `api/` and depend on package 03, and a draft change; package 03 finished on the default branch

**End state:**

- item 12 is `landing`; the fake hub's change is `open` at version 2 with `nightshift-gate` and `nightshift-review` both `passed` on version 2
- the item's thread holds, in this order, the entries `ready -> implementing`, `outside the plan: docs/api.md`, the two check entries and `reviewing -> landing`
- one new item of kind `defect` in `new` is linked to item 12
- the fake hub received no approval and no land request

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/daemon/e2e_test.go, with its startDaemon helper: seed item 12; eventually cli(['item','show','12']) contains 'state: landing'; assert fakeHub.Change('demo', n) == {state: 'open', version: 2}; assert fakeHub.Check(n, 'nightshift-gate').status == 'passed' and fakeHub.Check(n, 'nightshift-review').status == 'passed', both on version 2; assert the kinds and texts of cli(['thread','show',id]) in order; assert cli(['item','list','demo','--state','new']) names one item; assert fakeHub.Approvals(n) is empty and fakeHub.Lands(n) is empty
```

### PATH-2: A reviewer objects three times and the person sides with the implementer

1. **reviewer** objects to version 2 of item 13 with a finding naming a file and a line
2. **nightshiftd** reports `nightshift-review` failed and starts the implementer as a rework with the finding
3. **implementer** fixes the finding, pushes version 3 and writes its reply into the result file
4. **nightshiftd** writes the reply to the thread, gates version 3 and asks for a review, and does the same once more after a second objection
5. **reviewer** objects to version 4, the third review without `agree`
6. **nightshiftd** opens a `review_disagreement` decision with the findings and the replies
7. **person** runs `nightshift decide <id> --option side_with_implementer`
8. **nightshift** sends the answer to the daemon's API
9. **nightshiftd** reports `nightshift-review` passed on version 4, the summary naming the decision, and moves the item to `landing`

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the nightshiftd run function with its scheduler, session service, item service, inbox, store and event log, internal/impl, internal/gate and internal/review with the real command runner and gitclone, package 05's change service against the fake hub, git against the fake hub's git endpoint, the nightshift client's run function

**Setup:**

- the daemon started in-process with the e2e helper of internal/daemon/e2e_test.go, sessions unisolated, against internal/hubtest
- a fake `claude` on PATH: a script the test writes that commits, marks the package's tasks done, pushes the branch and writes the result file the step's prompt names
- the reviewer's provider is a provider/faux client scripted with the verdicts of the flow
- a fake `speca` on PATH that prints a gate envelope with the verdict the test sets
- item 13 seeded `reviewing` with a change at version 2 whose gate passed
- the faux provider scripted with three `object` verdicts

**End state:**

- the decision is answered and item 13 is `landing`
- the fake hub holds `nightshift-review` `failed` on versions 2 and 3 and `passed` on version 4 with the summary `passed by the owner's decision: side_with_implementer`
- the item's thread holds two `reply` entries and the decision with its answer
- the fake hub received no approval, and no request bore the approver token

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/daemon/e2e_test.go: seed item 13; eventually cli(['inbox','--action']) names a review_disagreement decision; assert cli(['decision','show',id]) holds the three findings and both replies; assert cli(['decide',id,'--option','side_with_implementer']).code == 0; eventually cli(['item','show','13']) contains 'state: landing'; assert fakeHub.Check(n, 'nightshift-review') per version; assert fakeHub.Approvals(n) is empty and fakeHub.RequestsWith(approverToken) is empty
```

### PATH-3: A blocked version waits for the person, its fork expires, and the answer restores and reworks it

1. **implementer** pushes a version of item 14 that touches `secrets/key.pem`
2. **hub** evaluates the version: the rule `nightshift-1` blocks the file
3. **nightshiftd** opens a `blocked` decision naming the rule and the file, and runs no gate
4. **hub** removes the item's fork at the end of its lifetime and abandons its change
5. **person** runs `nightshift decide <id> --option revise --comment "drop the key file"`
6. **nightshiftd** creates a new fork and a new change at the last version's head, names both changes in the thread, and starts the implementer as a rework with the comment as a binding finding
7. **implementer** removes the file and pushes
8. **nightshiftd** evaluates the new version without a block, runs the gate, reports `nightshift-gate` passed and moves the item to `reviewing`

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the nightshiftd run function with its scheduler, session service, item service, inbox, store and event log, internal/impl, internal/gate and internal/review with the real command runner and gitclone, package 05's change service against the fake hub, git against the fake hub's git endpoint, the nightshift client's run function

**Setup:**

- the daemon started in-process with the e2e helper of internal/daemon/e2e_test.go, sessions unisolated, against internal/hubtest
- a fake `claude` on PATH: a script the test writes that commits, marks the package's tasks done, pushes the branch and writes the result file the step's prompt names
- the reviewer's provider is a provider/faux client scripted with the verdicts of the flow
- a fake `speca` on PATH that prints a gate envelope with the verdict the test sets
- the fake hub's policy holds a rule `nightshift-1` that blocks `secrets/**`
- item 14 seeded `ready`; the fake claude's first run adds `secrets/key.pem`, its rework run removes it
- the test removes the fork on the fake hub as an expiry does, after the decision opened

**End state:**

- item 14 is `reviewing` on a new change whose fork is not the first one
- the first change is `abandoned` on the fake hub and has no check result; the new one has `nightshift-gate` `passed` on its last version
- the item's thread holds the `blocked` decision with its answer and the entry `fork expired: change demo#<old> continues as demo#<new>`
- the rework's findings file held one finding of the source `person` with `binding` true and the comment

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/daemon/e2e_test.go: seed item 14; eventually cli(['inbox','--action']) names a blocked decision; assert fakeHub.Checks(old) is empty; fakeHub.ExpireFork(oldFork); assert cli(['decide',id,'--option','revise','--comment','drop the key file']).code == 0; eventually cli(['item','show','14']) contains 'state: reviewing'; assert fakeHub.Change('demo', old).state == 'abandoned'; new = the item's change; assert new != old and fakeHub.Check(new, 'nightshift-gate').status == 'passed'; assert the thread contains 'fork expired: change demo#' + old + ' continues as demo#' + new; assert the findings file the fake claude recorded == [{id: 'blocked-' + id, source: 'person', text: 'drop the key file', binding: true}]
```

## External APIs

### `Parley REST API (agent-fox-dev/parley, docs/api.md)` (commit 7eabfb9) — verified

| Symbol | Import Path | Signature | Notes |
|--------|-------------|-----------|-------|
| `GET …/changes/{number}` | `<hub.endpoint>/api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/changes/{number}` | `scope changes:read (satisfied by changes:write); query include=versions,overlaps,approvals,checks; 200 change object {number, ref, title, intent, state: draft\|open\|landed\|abandoned, source: {workspace_slug, branch}, version: int, head_sha, base_sha, paths: [string] (at most 2,000), paths_truncated, landing: {status: ready\|pending\|blocked, reason, requirements: [{rule, paths (first 50), approvals: {required, counted, approvers}, checks: [{name, status}], block: bool, satisfied: bool}]}, versions?: [{number, head_sha, base_sha, kind, created_at}], overlaps?: [overlap entry]}` |  |
| `PATCH …/changes/{number}` | `<hub.endpoint>/api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/changes/{number}` | `scope changes:write; body {"state": "open"} marks a draft ready (the intent rule must hold), {"state": "draft"} turns it back; 200 with the change object` |  |
| `PUT …/changes/{number}/checks/{name}` | `<hub.endpoint>/api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/changes/{number}/checks/{name}` | `scope checks:write; a token bound to a task fork gets 403 token_bound; body {status: pending\|passed\|failed (required), version: int, summary: string of at most 2,000 characters, url?, details?}; one result per version and name, a report replaces the earlier one whole; 200 with the check` |  |
| `GET …/changes/{number}/diff` | `<hub.endpoint>/api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/changes/{number}/diff` | ``scope changes:read; query version=<n>\|latest, format=json\|patch, patches=true\|false; without `against` the diff from the version's base_sha to its head_sha; format=patch answers text/x-diff, cut at 8 MiB with the header X-Parley-Truncated: true; 404 not_found for a version the change does not have, 404 ref_not_found when its commits are gone`` |  |
| `GET …/changes/{number}/overlaps` | `<hub.endpoint>/api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/changes/{number}/overlaps` | ``one overlap entry per other draft or open change with the same target branch and a file in common: {change: {number, ref, title, state, version, …}, paths (first 100), paths_truncated, count}; empty for a landed or abandoned change; 404 change_not_found; the same entries as the member `overlaps` of GET …/changes/{number}?include=overlaps`` |  |
| `version ref` | `refs/parley/changes/<number>/<version>` | `the head of each version, kept in the target workspace's repository also for a fork source and after the fork is gone; a task fork reads its parent's objects` |  |
| `PATCH /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}` | `<hub.endpoint>/api/v1/workspaces/{slug}` | `for a task fork, body {"ttl": "7d"} (a whole number and m, h or d, from 5m to [forks].max_ttl) sets expires_at to now plus ttl; 400 invalid_request on a repository workspace; 200 with the workspace object` |  |
| `GET …/scm/file` | `<hub.endpoint>/api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/scm/file` | `scope git:read (satisfied by git:write); query path (required), ref (a revision; default the default branch); 200 the file's bytes as application/octet-stream; 404 path_not_found` |  |
| `POST …/scm/refs` | `<hub.endpoint>/api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/scm/refs` | `scope git:write; body {name: <branch>, sha: <full commit id>}; 201 with the ref object; 404 ref_not_found, 409 ref_exists` |  |
| `POST …/scm/commits` | `<hub.endpoint>/api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/scm/commits` | `scope git:write; body {branch, base_ref (required when the branch does not exist), message, operations: [{op: "put", path, content \| content_base64}]}; makes one commit and creates or moves the branch` |  |
| `POST …/changes` | `<hub.endpoint>/api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/changes` | `refuses with 400 nothing_to_land a source branch that has no commit the target lacks, and with 409 change_exists a branch that is the source of a draft or open change (called through package 05)` |  |

# Tasks

## Test Commands

- **all_tests:** `go test ./... -count=1`
- **linter:** `go vet ./...`
- **spec_tests:** `go test ./internal/impl/... ./internal/gate/... ./internal/review/... ./internal/hub/... ./internal/hubtest/... ./internal/daemon/... -count=1`

## Dependencies

- `01` — uses its configuration struct, store migrations, hub client with the worker credential, fake hub internal/hubtest, event log with Subscribe and the e2e helper
- `02` — runs the gate through command.Runner, clones the fork at a version with gitclone.Sync and reads the workspace with workspace.Service
- `03` — moves items with Transition, creates linked items with CreateLinked, abandons with Abandon, and declares, opens and answers decisions and writes thread entries through internal/inbox
- `04` — runs implementer and reviewer sessions through Scheduler.RunSession with session.Spec and its accept function, registers its steps and its start guard, records failures and reads Paused and OnResume
- `05` — creates the item's task fork and draft change and reads their record through change.Service (EnsureFork, OpenDraft, Get, Forget), reads the package directory and kept text from plan.Service.Kept, and registers its fork restore with plan.Service.RegisterPrepare

## Tasks

### 1. Read changes and packages from the hub, hold a ready item back for its dependencies and start its implementer (implement)

Take the names package 05 already gave to a call it added, and add only what is missing

### 2. Accept an implementer session from the hub's state and turn its open items into linked items (implement)

### 3. Keep findings, start reworks with them and decide what an implementing item needs next (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-2

**Steps:**

- 3.1 Add the rework behaviours to internal/impl/rework_test.go and the step order to internal/impl/step_test.go and confirm they fail
- 3.2 Add impl.Finding (ID, Source, Text, File, Line, Criterion, Output, Binding) and Rework(ctx, item, findings): validate every finding before storing any (ErrInvalid), refuse an unknown item and an item outside ready, implementing, reviewing and landing (ErrState), give a finding without an ID the next `f<n>` of the item, set Binding for the source person, skip an ID the item already has, append them in one transaction, move a reviewing or landing item to implementing with the reason `rework: <n> findings (<sources in order, each once>)`, and call the scheduler's Wake
- 3.3 Add Waiting(item) and History(item): the findings not yet given to an accepted rework, in their order, and the ones that were, each with its reply
- 3.4 Add the rework session: write the waiting findings as one JSON array to the input `findings`, each object with id, source, text and only the members that are set, and ask RunSession with the step name `implement` and the prompt `/af-impl <package directory> --unattended --rework {input:findings} --result {result}`, remembering which findings the session was given
- 3.5 Write the rework's accept function: first append one thread entry of the kind `reply` per entry of the result's `replies` (`<id> <action>: <text>`, cut to 2,000 characters, not unread) and store each reply with its finding; then compare the change's version with the one at the session's start: not greater is the error `no new version`, and the findings keep waiting
- 3.6 After an accepted rework move the findings it was given to the history, call HandleResult for its open items, and go on to the evaluation of the new version
- 3.7 Register the step for the state implementing: in a loop, do the first that applies and stop when a session ended otherwise than completed, a decision of the item is open, an error occurred or the item left implementing: RestoreFork (task 6 fills it; until then it returns nil); a check report not yet taken, with what follows its verdict; a `--no-merge` session when the item has no change or the package at the change's head is not finished; a rework when findings wait; the evaluation of a current version not yet evaluated; the gate for a version without a verdict; Transition to reviewing when the gate passed on the current version. Evaluation, report and gate are functions task 4 fills
- 3.8 Use one function for the states ready and implementing after the session was asked, so that the call that started as a ready step goes on as an implementing one
- 3.9 Add SetClass(ctx, item, class), stored with the item, and put the stored class into every sched.Request this package builds

### 4. Evaluate every version, open the blocked decision, note files outside the plan and overlaps, and run the gate (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-3

**Steps:**

- 4.1 Add the gate's verdict table to internal/gate/gate_test.go and the evaluation, gate, report and overlap behaviours to internal/impl/evaluate_test.go, with a helper in internal/gate that writes a fake `speca` script into a directory put first on PATH (it records its arguments, working directory and XDG_STATE_HOME and prints what the test gives it), and confirm they fail
- 4.2 Add the configuration key `gate.timeout` (a duration, default 30m) to internal/config, failing the config check with `config: gate.timeout must be greater than 0`
- 4.3 Add internal/gate: Run(ctx, Options{Runner, Dir, Package, Timeout, StateDir, ReadFile}) runs `speca <Package> --gate full --timeout <Timeout>` with `sh -c` through the command.Runner in Dir, with XDG_STATE_HOME set to an empty directory it makes under StateDir and removes afterwards, the JSON redirected to a file beside it that it reads with ReadFile (package 04's file read as the session user) and removes; the command's own limit is twice Timeout plus one minute; it returns Verdict{Passed, Summary, Tail} and an error only when the context was cancelled
- 4.4 Map everything but the verdict `pass` to Passed false: the summary is the envelope's `summary`, or `gate did not run: speca exited <N>`, `gate did not run: no verdict in speca's output` or `gate did not run: timed out`, followed for a failed command by a line `<name> exited <code>` (`<name> timed out`) and its tail; cut the whole to 2,000 characters; add the constant CheckName `nightshift-gate`
- 4.5 Add ReportCheck to the hub client (PUT …/checks/{name} with status, version and summary) and to internal/hubtest the check route with an accessor and a way to make it answer 503; add (*impl.Service).ReportCheck(ctx, item, name, status, summary): cut the summary to 2,000 characters, store the report as pending, send it for the change's current version, append the thread entry of the kind `check` (`<name> <status> on version <v>: <summary>`) once the hub took it, and leave it pending with the error otherwise; the implementing step sends a pending report before anything else
- 4.6 Add Version(ctx, item): the item's change read with include=overlaps as impl.Version (Workspace, Change, Number, HeadSHA, BaseSHA, State, Paths, Requirements, Overlaps)
- 4.7 Fill the evaluation: for a version not yet evaluated, when a requirement has block, call OpenBlocked and record the version as evaluated; otherwise compute the files outside the plan from the package's touches at the version's head (an entry equal to the path, or a directory above it compared by whole path segments, or the package's own directory), store the list, and append the `outside_plan` entry when the list is not empty and differs from the last one written (the first 50 in path order joined with `, `, then ` and <n> more`); add OutsidePlan(ctx, item)
- 4.8 Declare the kind `blocked` with the inbox's RegisterKind (`revise`: `starts the implementer with your comment`, comment required; `abandon`: `ends the item without landing`) and add OpenBlocked(ctx, item, reqs): one decision per version, with the question, the change's URL and each blocking rule with its files as evidence, `revise` recommended and `item <N>` blocked
- 4.9 Register the `blocked` handlers with OnAnswer: `revise` calls Rework with the finding `blocked-<decision id>` of the source person and the comment; `abandon` calls the item service's Abandon; register them through (*impl.Service).OnAnswer(kind, option, fn), which wraps the inbox's OnAnswer: when Scheduler.Paused says the item is paused it stores the answer and returns nil, and a function registered with Scheduler.OnResume carries the stored answers out in order; task 5 registers its kind through it too
- 4.10 Fill the gate step: bring <sessions.dir>/items/<N>/gate to the version's head with gitclone.Sync from the fork's git URL and the worker token, call gate.Run, store the verdict with the version before anything is reported, then ReportCheck; what follows a verdict is done once, after the hub took its report, also when that happens at a later step: on a pass set the count of failed gates in a row to zero and move the item to reviewing
- 4.11 On a failed gate, after its report was taken, call Rework with one finding of the source gate (the summary's first line, the tail as output) and count it: the first in a row is given to Scheduler.RecordFailure(ctx, item, `implement`, `gate failed: <first line>`, ``), the second, with no passed gate between, to Scheduler.OpenSessionFailed with both failures
- 4.12 After every gate read the change's overlap entries and append an `overlap` entry (`overlaps change <workspace>#<number>`) for each other change not yet stored as noted for the item; describe `gate.timeout` in docs/configuration.md

### 5. Review every gated version and take a disagreement to the person (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-4

**Steps:**

- 5.1 Add the review behaviours to internal/review/review_test.go, over the real impl service and a stub scheduler whose RunSession returns the verdict the test scripts, and confirm they fail
- 5.2 Add ChangeDiff(ctx, slug, number, version) to the hub client (GET …/diff with format=patch, answering the text and whether the hub cut it) and the route to internal/hubtest, served from its repositories
- 5.3 Add internal/review with the step for the state reviewing, registered with Scheduler.RegisterStep: call impl's RestoreFork; send a pending check report first; read impl's Version; when impl holds no passed gate for the current version, move the item to implementing with the reason `version <v> is not gated` and return
- 5.4 Build the prompt: the review brief, the package's directory, the version's files, the diff up to 400,000 characters and the line `diff cut: <n> characters left out` when it was cut, the gate's stored summary, every finding of impl's History that came from a review with its reply's action and text, and the form of the verdict object package 04 expects
- 5.5 Ask Scheduler.RunSession for a reviewer session with the step name `review`, the fork, the version's head as Commit, the item's class and an accept function that refuses a verdict `object` with a finding that has neither a file with a line nor a criterion (`finding names no file and line and no criterion`); return nil on sched.ErrNotStarted and on an outcome other than completed
- 5.6 Store the verdict and its findings with the version before reporting. On `agree`: impl's ReportCheck with CheckName `nightshift-review`, `passed` and `reviewer agrees`, the count of reviews without agree set to zero, Transition to landing
- 5.7 On `object`: ReportCheck `failed` with `reviewer objects: <n> findings` and the findings' texts, add one to the count; below 3, call impl's Rework with the findings as findings of the source review
- 5.8 At a count of 3 or more open the decision instead: declare the kind `review_disagreement` with RegisterKind (`side_with_reviewer`: `gives the implementer one more session with the findings as binding`; `side_with_implementer`: `passes the review on your word`; `abandon`: `ends the item without landing`), and open it with the question, the change's URL, each finding of this review and each earlier review finding with its reply as evidence, `side_with_reviewer` recommended
- 5.9 Register the three handlers through impl's OnAnswer: `side_with_reviewer` calls Rework with the last review's findings, Binding set, ids `review-<decision id>-<index>`; `side_with_implementer` reports `nightshift-review` passed with `passed by the owner's decision: side_with_implementer` and moves the item to landing unless it is there already; `abandon` calls Abandon
- 5.10 Send no request to the approvals route anywhere in this package and never use the approver credential; build the review step in daemon.Run and give it to the e2e helper

### 6. Extend the forks of running items, restore an expired fork, and prove the flows end to end (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-5

**Steps:**

- 6.1 Add the fork behaviours to internal/impl/forks_test.go and confirm they fail
- 6.2 Add SetForkTTL(ctx, fork, ttl), CreateRef(ctx, slug, name, sha) and Commit(ctx, slug, branch, baseRef, message, files) to the hub client, and to internal/hubtest the PATCH of a fork's ttl, POST scm/refs, POST scm/commits and ExpireFork(slug), which removes a fork as the hub's expiry does: the fork answers 404, its draft and open changes are abandoned and their versions stay readable in the parent
- 6.3 Add ExtendForks(ctx): for every item of the item service's List that has a fork record, is neither done nor abandoned and has a null waiting_on, call SetForkTTL with `7d`; log a refusal with the item's number and go on; run it at the daemon's start and on a ticker of 6 hours, both injected, in a goroutine that stops with the daemon
- 6.4 Add RestoreFork(ctx, item): return nil for an item without a fork record and for a fork the hub answers 200 for; on 404 restore, one item at a time
- 6.5 Restore an item that is not awaiting_approval: read the earlier change with include=versions and keep its number, title, intent and last version's head in the store before anything is created; call package 05's change.Service.Forget and EnsureFork, which gives the fork `i<N>-<g>`; CreateRef for the branch of the new record at that head; OpenDraft with the kept title and intent and no session id; SetChangeState open for an item in implementing, reviewing or landing; append the `fork_restored` entry; move a reviewing or landing item to implementing with the reason `fork restored`. An item without an earlier change gets the fork alone
- 6.6 Restore an item that is awaiting_approval: Forget and EnsureFork, then Commit the files of package 05's plan.Service.Kept under its Dir to the item's branch with the fork's default branch as base and the message `plan for item <N>`, OpenDraft, and the entry; the state stays
- 6.7 Record each finished step of a restore with the item, so that a restore that failed part-way goes on at the next trigger without creating a second fork, branch, change or entry
- 6.8 Trigger RestoreFork from the event-log follower of task 1 on decision.answered with an option other than `abandon` (the event's data names the item and the option), from the function registered with package 05's plan.Service.RegisterPrepare under the name `fork`, and at the start of the steps for ready, implementing and reviewing
- 6.9 Add the three flows to internal/daemon/e2e_test.go with its startDaemon helper, a fake claude that pushes and writes result files per prompt, a fake speca and a faux reviewer
- 6.10 Add to docs/architecture.md the packages internal/impl, internal/gate and internal/review, the order in which a step decides what to do, and what later packages use: Rework, SetClass, ReportCheck, Version, OpenBlocked, OnAnswer, RestoreFork, OutsidePlan, gate.Run and the hub client's change calls; add to docs/api.md the decision kinds `blocked` and `review_disagreement` with their options and the thread entry kinds `check`, `reply`, `outside_plan`, `overlap` and `fork_restored`; name the fake `speca` helper and the new routes of internal/hubtest under Repository Specifics in .specs/steering.md; run `make doc`
